card.name: Digits inside toll-free phone numbers
card.fires_on: The repeated digit (6, 8 or 0) in the area-code part of a toll-free number such as 1-888 or 1-866, after 1- or 'call'. It appears in contact lines for reporting side effects, REMS programs and poison control.

modes.label: Adverse event reporting line
modes.description: Last digit of an 800-series prefix in a line telling readers whom to contact to report a problem or get information.
modes.example: Report any diagnosis of NSF following AMBELVIST administration to Bayer HealthCare (1- 88<<8>>-842-293

modes.label: REMS or program phone number
modes.description: The 888 or 866 prefix after a REMS website or call center mention.
modes.example: EXUS REMS is available at www.ZENBEXUSREMS.com or by calling the REMS Call Center at 1-88<<8>>-423-543

modes.label: Poison control number
modes.description: The 800 prefix in an overdose instruction.
modes.example: In case of overdose, call Poison Control Center at 1-80<<0>>-222-122

card.plain: It fires on the repeated digit in the 800/888/866 start of a toll-free number in a contact line.
